item.title: How to Migrate n8n from npm to Docker Before n8n 3.0
item.description:
Introduction

If you run n8n from npx n8n or a global npm install n8n -g, your installation has an expiry date. n8n 3.0, scheduled for October 2026, drops support for npm-based installs entirely, and the n8n package on npm stops at the last 2.x release. This guide migrates a working npm install to Docker Compose without losing workflows, credentials, or execution history. It is written for self-hosters on a VPS or home server who installed n8n the quick way years ago and now need the supported path. If you followed our Ubuntu VPS install guide, the backup habits from that post apply here too.

item.title: n8n 3.0 Upgrade Guide: The Breaking Changes Checklist Before You Update
item.description:
Introduction

n8n 3.0, scheduled for October 2026, is the most disruptive release in the project’s recent history. It ends npm and npx installs for self-hosters, removes more than 35 legacy nodes and helpers, retires Chat Hub, and tightens security defaults that change how Code nodes, community packages, and webhooks behave. This guide is the pre-upgrade checklist for anyone running a production 2.x instance, on Docker or npm, who owns workflows that must keep working the morning after the upgrade. If you have not yet moved off npm, read our npm to Docker migration guide alongside this one, because that move is now mandatory.

item.title: How to Fix n8n CVE-2026-44791: Patch the XML Node Prototype Pollution Bypass
item.description:
Introduction

If you self-host n8n, there is a critical patch you need to apply. In May 2026, n8n published security advisory GHSA-wrwr-h859-xh2r for CVE-2026-44791, an XML node prototype pollution bypass rated CVSS 4.0 9.4 Critical. An authenticated user with permission to create or modify workflows can dodge the earlier XML node fix and, combined with other nodes, reach remote code execution on the n8n host. This guide walks you through checking whether your instance is vulnerable, applying the emergency workaround, upgrading on Docker and npm, locking down permissions, and verifying the fix. It is written for anyone who runs their own n8n, from a single Docker container on a VPS to a multi-worker queue mode cluster. If you installed n8n with our Ubuntu VPS install guide, start at Step 1.

item.title: How to Update n8n Self-Hosted: Safe Upgrades for Docker Compose, Docker, and npm (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Updating self-hosted n8n is where most self-hosting horror stories start: a skipped backup, a jumped migration, a dead credential set. This guide shows the safe update path for all three install methods, Docker Compose, plain Docker, and npm, with the exact commands, the pre-update backup routine, and the rollback procedure from n8n’s own documentation. It is written for anyone already running n8n on their own server, and pairs with our guide to installing n8n on an Ubuntu VPS and our Docker Compose setup walkthrough if you set things up with our tutorials.

item.title: n8n Docker Compose Setup: Self-Hosting with Postgres and Queue Mode (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Docker Compose is the way n8n’s own team ships production deployments, and it is the only install path n8n guarantees going forward. This guide builds a complete, production-ready docker-compose.yml for n8n: Postgres as the database, named volumes for data, a .env file for secrets, optional queue mode with Redis workers for heavier workloads, and a safe upgrade routine. It works on any host with Docker, from a $6 VPS to a homelab box. If you need the full VPS walkthrough with a domain and HTTPS in front of this setup, read our guide to installing n8n on an Ubuntu VPS first, it ends exactly where this article begins.

item.title: How to Install n8n on Ubuntu VPS (2026): Docker Compose, Postgres & Free HTTPS
item.description:
Introduction

Self-hosting n8n on a cheap Ubuntu VPS is the single biggest cost lever in workflow automation: the same agent workloads that cost hundreds per month on per-operation platforms run for the price of a $6 VPS. This guide walks you through the production-ready setup, Docker Compose, Postgres 18, and free HTTPS via Caddy, on Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04. Every command below is real, the compose file follows n8n’s official hosting examples, and the n8n behavior notes come from actually running n8n 2.40.7 locally.
